summary: Request for adjustment: unexpected burst metering from mixed-priority queue during weekend workload
description:
Issue summary:
Customer FitAssist reported a sudden weekend spike in billable token usage attributed to a burst window on their dedicated pool. They noticed the spike coincided with a scheduled batch job and an out-of-hours traffic surge. Customer believes some tokens were double-counted when requests were routed between mixed-priority queues (interactive + batch).

Impact:
- Unexpected ~$3.2k charge on invoice dated 2026-03-09 for weekend usage window (period 2026-03-07 to 2026-03-08).
- Customer currently on Dedicated plan with reserved capacity and burst-of-spot enabled. This is a material billing concern for finance and the customer’s procurement.

Timeline (provided by customer):
- 2026-03-07 22:10 UTC: scheduled nightly batch launches (batch queue).
- 2026-03-07 22:12 UTC: sudden increase in interactive traffic from QA run (interactive queue).
- 2026-03-07 22:12–22:45 UTC: spike in metering events and token counts recorded in billing export (attached by customer).
- 2026-03-09: customer received invoice with unexplained line item "Burst Capacity - emergency".

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Run a small interactive workload from dev host while a larger batch job runs.
2) Observe per-request routing to mixed-priority queues with fallback to burst capacity when reserved pool nears saturation.
3) Export metering usage for the time window; customer sees repeated entries for same request IDs with different route tags.

Logs / Observations from customer (attached):
- CSV of usage events showing duplicated request_id values across two route tags: "interactive" and "batch-fallback".
- Sample API traces showing a single client request that retried and then completed; both attempts appear billed.

Expected behavior:
- Retries or fallbacks should be deduplicated for billing where they correspond to the same logical request within X seconds (configurable), or at least attributed to the original route without double-counting token consumption.

Additional context:
- Customer uses prefix caching for interactive requests and larger sequence lengths for batch jobs. They enabled burst-on-demand in their dedicated pool to absorb spikes. They prefer a billing adjustment for the weekend spike and guidance on configuration to avoid recurrence.
comments: 2026-03-10 | Support (Aisha Patel): Acknowledged receipt and opened SUP-36321. Asked customer for invoice number, CSV of usage export, and example request IDs. Noted SLA window. Status: Triage.

2026-03-10 | Customer (FitAssist - billing@fitassist.com): Provided invoice INV-2026-03-09-772 and CSV with 18 candidate request_ids. Customer requests credit for duplicate-billed tokens and a short RCA so they can explain to procurement.

2026-03-10 | Support (Luis Navarro): Escalated to infra/metering. Linked INT-4271 to surface recent changes to mixed-queue routing. Requested meter team to check deduplication and billing attribution logic; attached PRs for recent routing changes.

2026-03-11 | Infra (SRE - Mei Chen): Confirmed detection of concurrent routing state during 2026-03-07 22:12 UTC window. Notes: an autoscaler event caused temporary overlap where requests were proxied to both interactive frontends and the batch runner for a small subset; meter wrote two usage events for the same internal correlation id. Working hypothesis: correlation_id was not propagated in one fallback path, preventing dedupe at billing aggregation stage.

2026-03-11 | Billing (Rajiv Singh): Tally of candidate duplicates yields ~98k tokens duplicated equating to $3,230. Proposing a manual credits adjustment and improving the aggregator to dedupe on correlation_id + request_hash for 30s windows.

2026-03-12 | Support (Luis Navarro): Applied a one-time invoice credit of $3,230 and created ticket BILL-1126 for accounting to post credit memo against INV-2026-03-09-772. Confirmed credit applied and customer notified. Recommend follow-ups to infra and metering teams for code fix and improved tests.
2026-03-12 | Customer (FitAssist): Acknowledged receipt of credit and thanked the team. Requests notice when fix is deployed and asks for recommended config changes to avoid recurrence.
investigation_notes:
Summary of technical findings:
- Root cause: race window caused by autoscaler + mixed-queue router change in infra PR #884 where in-flight requests could be proxied through two code paths. The metering agent emitted two usage events for the same logical request because the fallback path did not preserve the original correlation_id header.
- Reproducer: synthetic test created that runs heavy batch traffic with intermittent interactive pings; confirmed duplicate events in local staging.
- Short-term mitigation: billing-side filter to dedupe events by correlation_id + truncated request_hash for 30s.
- Long-term fix: change in router to always copy correlation_id into fallback requests and add unit/integration tests (metering PR #210).
resolution:
Action taken: Applied a one-time credit for $3,230. Accounting ticket BILL-1126 created to attach credit memo to the customer's invoice. Infra changes: merged hotfix to ensure correlation_id is copied into fallback routes (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/884) and metering aggregator updated to dedupe within 30s windows (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/metering/pull/210).
Preventative steps: add e2e test harness for mixed-queue routing, update runbooks to temporarily disable burst-on-demand for vulnerable pools during large scheduled batch jobs, and notify customers about recommended config (set burst-grace-period to 60s).
Follow-up: Monitor billing export for two weeks post-deploy; assigned INT-4271 for infra verification and BILL-1126 for finance closure. Customer confirmed refund/credit received on 2026-03-12. Ticket closed.
public_resolution_note: We identified a short race condition in the routing layer that caused some requests to be billed twice during an autoscaler event. We issued a credit for the duplicated usage and deployed fixes to prevent recurrence. If you see any further unexpected charges, please reply and we'll investigate immediately.
